newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Man dies in Geneva airport shooting after theft.
newsitem.headline: Man dies in Geneva airport shooting after theft.

text.p: A 19-year-old asylum seeker from Serbia's Kosovo province died on Monday after a policeman opened fire following a theft at Geneva airport involving thousands of dollars, a police spokesman said.
The incident occurred in an underground car park at the Cointrin international terminal just after 7 a.m. (0500 GMT), spokesman Jacques Volery told a news conference.

He said the policeman went to the car park after a briefcase was snatched from an Arab traveller -- who later said it contained several thousand dollars -- just after he arrived by taxi to catch a flight.
"The officer saw three people bent over a briefcase and called on them to give themselves up," said Volery, "but one of them appeared to take a black object from his waist and point it."

The policeman opened fire, hitting the man in the chest, and the other two ran away, apparently with the money in the briefcase, which was found empty. The injured man died soon after being rushed to hospital.

Volery did not identify the dead man. He said he had applied for asylum in February after arriving in Switzerland in January, but was under a preliminary expulsion order after having been held by police in connection with other airport thefts.
No weapon was found at the site of the incident, according to the spokesman. The Arab passenger, who was also not identified, filed charges over the loss of his money.
Volery said there had been an upsurge of similar thefts this year at Cointrin, one of Switzerland's two main international airports and a busy hub for many European airlines.
So far this year, there had been 246 baggage snatchings, 188 of them of briefcases, he said.
